newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts sees products back Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts sees products back Wednesday.

text.p: Arnotts Ltd said on Tuesday that following advice from police the company would return its products to supermarket shelves from Wednesday morning.
Queensland Police said earlier they were confident there was no longer a threat to food items as a result of the extortion threat against the bakery group.

"Following advice from the Queensland and New South Wales police it is appropriate for us to return our products to the shelves," Arnotts chief executive Chris Roberts told reporters. "From 6 a.m. (2030 GMT) tomorrow morning our products will be back on the shelves in New South Wales and Queensland."
Roberts said the company's biscuits would not be in tamper-proof packaging as hoped.
"It has been our long term aim to get tamper-proof products across our range but we have no timetable for this," he said.
"We are absolutely certain that it is now safe to return our products to the shelves."
He said it would take a number of weeks to fill the shelves of supermarkets in the two states.
"We have a huge task ahead of us. It will take several weeks to restore our products. I regret there will be a shortage of products for some time."
Arnotts withdrew its products on February 14 after the company was embroiled in a complicated extortion scandal involving a convicted murderer and police.
Shares in Arnotts, which is controlled by Campbell Soup Co, were five cents lower at A$8.85 at 4.00 p.m. (0500 GMT).
